explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/467: 'Prove the following for all large x: there is a choice of congruence classes a_p for all primes p ≤ x and a decomposition {p ≤ x} = A ⊔ B into two non-empty sets such that, for all n < x, there exist some p ∈ A and q ∈ B such that n ≡ a_p (mod p) and n ≡ a_q (mod q).' The Lean statement: for all sufficiently large x there exist residue : ℕ → ℕ and finsets A, B, nonempty, disjoint, with union the primes ≤ x, such that every n < x satisfies n % p = residue p % p for some p ∈ A and n % q = residue q % q for some q ∈ B. This is exactly the page's interpretation (which the page itself flags as a reconstruction of an under-quantified original). Faithful to the cited source.
